claims.text: High-entropy alloys with controlled chemical short-range order can exhibit enhanced glass-forming ability.
The relevant high-entropy alloys may initially be amorphous or crystalline.
Adding elements such as Cr, V, and Hf is a potential intervention for enhancing glass-forming ability in high-entropy alloys.
Controlling chemical short-range order is a potential intervention for enhancing glass-forming ability in high-entropy alloys.
Cooling and solidification conditions are relevant to the proposed enhancement of glass-forming ability.
Controlled chemical short-range order may alter atomic arrangement in high-entropy alloys.
Controlled chemical short-range order may alter atomic bonding in high-entropy alloys.
Changes in atomic arrangement and bonding caused by controlled short-range order may enhance glass-forming ability.
The proposed improvement in glass-forming ability depends on the specific high-entropy-alloy composition.
The proposed improvement in glass-forming ability depends on processing conditions.
The exact relationship between chemical short-range order and glass-forming ability is not fully understood.
